brief: Equity markets sold off last week on AI valuation concerns: Nvidia slumped despite strong earnings after fresh reports of an SEC accounting probe, and Anthropic's record IPO gave back most of its debut gains. That triggered broader de-leveraging, and gold, as a highly liquid asset, got caught in the resulting risk reduction, with XAU falling 8.9% to Friday's close and breaking key Fibonacci support at $3,858 to test $3,500, a 37% drop from this year's peak. ETF outflows, COMEX long liquidation and rising demand for downside options protection accompanied the fall, though sticky ETF holdings and China's SHFE position were little changed. WGC's near-term bias is for a bounce, since commodity positioning looks stretched and Polymarket odds have swung toward a rebound to $3,700, but its broader bias stays negative because the dollar looks to have based and turned higher and the Fed stays hawkish (minutes show broad support for a December hike), even as fewer hikes are now priced for 2027. The S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and MSCI AC World all broke key technical supports in the same risk-off move. Bottom line: a broad reduction in risk exposure is dragging liquid assets down; a bounce is possible, but caution is still warranted since no clear positioning washout has yet appeared.
